name: Maria Rodriguez
current_role: Trauma nurse and small business owner
bio: Maria Teresa Rodriguez is the Republican nominee for Kentucky's 3rd congressional district. Born and raised in Cuba, she came to the United States at 21 after a lengthy asylum process, later became a citizen, started a small business and earned a nursing degree. She works as a trauma nurse in Louisville.

platform.point: Lists safer streets in Louisville as a top priority.
Promotes lower taxes and defending capitalism and free enterprise.
Says the border should be secured and laws enforced while keeping an immigration system for those who follow the rules.
Emphasizes legal immigration as a campaign priority, drawing on her own path from Cuba.
Lists protecting the unborn among her priorities.
Pledges to protect women's sports.

economy.evidence: General statement: campaign lists lower taxes and defending capitalism and free enterprise as priorities, without specific proposals.

liberty.evidence: General statements: campaign priorities include protecting the unborn (abortion) and protecting women's sports (LGBTQ issues), without further detail.

security.evidence: General statement: campaign lists safe streets and a safer Louisville as priorities, without specific policing proposals.

immigration.evidence: General statement: says the country must secure its borders and enforce its laws while preserving a system for immigrants who follow the rules.

notes: Searched her campaign site, iVoterGuide (she answered no questions), local news and a WHAS11 interview listing (Trump, tariffs, immigration) whose content could not be read; the Kentucky Lantern voter guide was blocked. Her site's news posts are template placeholders, and no positions were found on welfare, foreign policy, energy, tech, education or faith.

name: Ned Pillersdorf
bio: Ned Pillersdorf is a Prestonsburg attorney who has practiced law for over four decades, much of it representing low-income clients, including thousands of eastern Kentuckians who lost disability benefits in the Eric Conn case. He was a candidate for this district in 1992 and is the 2026 Democratic nominee against Rep. Hal Rogers.

platform.point: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps, utility assistance and job training.
Wants to expand health care access, protect rural hospitals and supports the Affordable Care Act.
Opposes further tax breaks for the wealthiest Americans that add to the deficit.
Prioritizes rural broadband and safe drinking water in eastern Kentucky.
Pledges to defend Social Security and disability benefits, including service staffing.
Opposes defunding public television, public radio, Job Corps and cancer research.
Supports uncapping the size of the House and term limits.

economy.evidence: Criticizes tax breaks for billionaires and opposes the 2025 budget law.

welfare.evidence: Opposes cuts to Medicaid, Medicare, food stamps and utility assistance, backs the Affordable Care Act and wants expanded health access.

education.evidence: General statement: criticizes federal cuts to education funding, Job Corps and pandemic relief reimbursements for rural schools.

notes: Searched his site's home, press release and media pages, launch coverage (WYMT, Spectrum, LEX18, Kentucky Lantern via Yahoo) and voter guides; his campaign focuses almost entirely on safety-net programs. No statements were found on abortion, guns, coal or energy, immigration, foreign policy, tech, policing or faith, and no headshot was found.

name: Ralph Alvarado
bio: Ralph Alvarado is a physician who served in the Kentucky State Senate from 2015 to 2023, the first Hispanic member of the Kentucky General Assembly, and was Tennessee's health commissioner from 2023 to 2025. He was Matt Bevin's running mate for lieutenant governor in 2019. He won the 2026 Republican primary for the open 6th district seat after an endorsement from President Trump.

platform.point: Wants more affordable care, clearer insurance choices and more patient control, working with both parties.
Focuses on lowering prices for groceries, gas and health care.
Aims to grow jobs in Kentucky.
Pledges to eliminate wasteful government spending to reduce inflation.
Campaign site pledged to secure the southern border and stop the flow of fentanyl.
Campaign site pledged to restore energy independence and cut taxes.
As a state senator, sponsored bills to create and expand education opportunity accounts for private school costs.
Sponsored state abortion bills in 2017 and 2020 and says life deserves legal protection from conception.

economy.evidence: Sponsored medical malpractice tort reform as a state senator and campaigns on cutting taxes and wasteful spending.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only: sponsored Kentucky abortion bills SB 5 (2017) and SB 9 (2020, born-alive infants) and strongly agreed that life deserves legal protection from conception.

immigration.evidence: Sponsored Kentucky SB 1 (2020) on cooperation with federal immigration enforcement, and his campaign pledged to secure the southern border.

energy.evidence: General statement: campaign site pledged to restore energy independence, without specific proposals.

education.evidence: As a state senator, introduced SB 50 (2022) to extend education opportunity accounts for private school costs to all counties and more middle-class families.

notes: Searched his campaign site, Kentucky legislature sponsor records, iVoterGuide (only one abortion answer), his 2022 legislative column and primary coverage; he skipped the League of Women Voters primary debate, and his current site no longer lists the border and energy pledges. No positions found on welfare, policing, foreign policy, tech or faith.

name: Randall Arrington
bio: Randall Arrington of Ponchatoula is a retired Navy aviator who spent about two decades as a Department of Homeland Security air interdiction agent and holds a doctorate in political science. He ran against Rep. Steve Scalise in 2024 and is running again in 2026.

platform.point: Calls for sealing the border and deporting people in the country illegally (2024 statement).
Wants the strongest military in the world and says war should be a last resort (2024 statement).
Says tax dollars should address Americans' problems rather than those of foreign nations (2024 statement).
Aims to end inflation, balance the federal budget and eliminate the national debt (2024 statement).
Describes himself as moderately pro-life, backs leaving abortion to states, and favors limits with exceptions for rape, incest and the mother's life.
Says veterans should receive the benefits they earned (2024 statement).

economy.evidence: General statement from 2024: lists ending inflation, balancing the budget and eliminating the national debt as goals.

liberty.evidence: Abortion only: in 2024 said government should not control a woman's body but the fetus needs protection, backing limits with rape, incest and life exceptions.

immigration.evidence: Listed sealing the border and deporting people in the country illegally among his goals in 2024.

foreign.evidence: In 2024 said tax dollars should serve Americans rather than foreign nations, war is a last resort and World War III must be prevented, while backing a strong military.

notes: Positions come from his own 2024 Vote-USA answers (dated October 2024) since no 2026 campaign site was found; sources differ on where he earned his doctorate. No statements found on welfare, policing, energy, tech, education or faith.

name: Renada Collins
current_role: TV host, Bigg Mouth Media Group
bio: Renada "Honey" Collins of New Orleans ran as an unaffiliated candidate for mayor of New Orleans in 2025. She first filed as a Democrat against Rep. Troy Carter in 2026 and is listed without party affiliation for the November 3 open primary.

platform.point: As a 2025 mayoral candidate, pledged to modernize operations, cut waste and use data-driven systems.
Said she would avoid new burdens on working families and cut inefficiencies before any tax changes.
Proposed coordinating infrastructure and public safety planning for streets, drainage and safer neighborhoods.

economy.evidence: General statement from her 2025 mayoral survey: would avoid tax burdens on working families and cut inefficiencies before changing taxes.

notes: Qualifying coverage (WRKF/WWNO, August 2026) lists her as NP (no party) although she filed as a Democrat for the canceled May primary, so the party label should be checked against race data. Her only policy answers found are local ones from a 2025 mayoral survey; the Verite News guide and Louisiana Illuminator were blocked, and no 2026 campaign site was found.

name: Caleb Walker
current_role: Community coordinator; student body president, South Louisiana Community College
bio: Caleb Walker served more than 10 years in the U.S. Army, reaching Sergeant First Class and deploying to Afghanistan. Originally from Wisner in Franklin Parish, he moved to Lafayette in 2020, worked as a Sam's Club department manager and is now a community coordinator. He studies political science at South Louisiana Community College, where he is student body president, and serves on the Louisiana Task Force for Career Alignment.

platform.point: Lower grocery, housing and insurance costs and push for wages that keep pace with the economy.
Raise teacher pay and exempt the first $50,000 of educator salaries from federal income tax.
Provide student-loan forgiveness for healthcare workers serving Louisiana.
Secure hazardous-duty pay for essential workers during declared natural disasters.
Fund coastal restoration, stronger flood protection and storm-resilient infrastructure.
Address global warming with science-based solutions, including responsible carbon-capture projects.
Wants FEMA resources and personnel positioned before storms arrive rather than after.
Called for replacing Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth with more experienced military leadership.

economy.evidence: General statement: calls for lower living costs and wages that keep pace, plus a targeted federal income tax exemption for teachers.

foreign.evidence: General statement: in a May 2026 forum said it is better to have a fight overseas than at home, and called for more experienced Pentagon leadership.

energy.evidence: Pledges science-based action on global warming, including carbon capture, while supporting Louisiana's energy industry.

education.evidence: Proposes raising teacher pay and exempting the first $50,000 of educator salaries from federal income tax.

notes: Searched his issues and about pages, American Press and WRKF coverage; the social links on his site are unfilled template placeholders and the Illuminator was blocked. No statements found on abortion, guns, immigration, healthcare policy, tech or faith; the campaign photo is assumed to be his home-page portrait.

name: Mike Nichols
bio: Mike Nichols of Pitkin is a retired land management and water resources specialist with more than 35 years of experience as a biologist. He is running as a Republican in the 4th District against incumbent Speaker Mike Johnson.

platform.point: Opposes carbon dioxide injection wells he says endanger drinking water for much of the region.
Proposes a plan to address eminent domain abuse in Louisiana.
Says he wants to boost local industry in the district.

notes: His site has only a slogan, two linked PDF flyers (not opened, per the no-download rule) and two embedded interview videos; platform points come from the description of one video interview he links. His carbon-well stance does not map onto the energy scale, and no other positions were found.

name: Conrad Cable
bio: Conrad Cable is a north Louisiana farmer who graduated from the University of Louisiana at Monroe in 2017 and started a farm in Union Parish with his brother after losing his job during the COVID-19 pandemic. He is running as a Democrat in the 4th District against Speaker Mike Johnson, campaigning on wages, health care and food security.

platform.point: Supports Medicare for All and opposes federal cuts to Medicaid.
Wants a minimum wage above $17 an hour by 2030, indexed to inflation, and an end to the tipped minimum wage.
Proposes public grocery stores in rural and low-income areas stocked with local food and accepting SNAP and WIC.
Backs overturning Citizens United, banning stock trading by members of Congress and lifetime lobbying bans.
Argues current farm and trade policy has hurt Louisiana soybean growers.
Supports paid family and medical leave with at least 14 weeks for mothers and 10 days for fathers.
Wants free school breakfast and lunch guaranteed for all children.
Calls for clean water access, rural fiber internet and flood insurance reform.

economy.evidence: Proposes a minimum wage above $17 by 2030, ending the tipped minimum wage, stronger union protections and publicly run grocery stores.

welfare.evidence: Supports Medicare for All, paid family leave and universal free school meals, and opposes Medicaid cuts.

notes: Searched his home, vision and bio pages, launch video, and Louisiana Radio Network and Yahoo coverage; his own site calls him a first-generation farmer, while some news reports say fifth-generation. He criticizes Johnson in religious terms, but no policy positions were found on abortion, guns, immigration, energy, foreign policy, tech, policing or religion in public life.
